market_question: Will the No to ten million Switzerland initiative be approved in Switzerland’s June 14, 2026 popular vote?
reasoning: The 'No to ten million Switzerland' initiative is a classic SVP immigration cap, similar to the 2020 limitation initiative (38.3% Yes) and the 2014 mass immigration initiative (50.3%), but the trend has been declining support. The government recommended rejection without a counter-proposal, citing economic harm and incompatibility with international agreements. The double‑majority requirement (popular and cantonal) makes passage very difficult, as the initiative likely only finds majority support in rural German‑speaking cantons. Historical SVP immigration initiatives since 2014 have rarely exceeded 40% and recent polling suggests around 25-30% Yes, making the market’s 33.5% implied probability slightly too high.
evidence_points: The 2020 limitation initiative (against EU free movement) failed with 38.3% Yes, a similar topic.
The Federal Council recommended rejecting the initiative without a counter-proposal, signaling weak elite and cross-party support.
Double majority requirement (people + cantons) further reduces the chance of passage, as only a handful of conservative cantons are likely to back it.
sources_consulted: Swiss Federal Chancellery voting records (2020 deprivation initiative results)
Federal Council press releases on the 'No to 10 million Switzerland' initiative (2024/2025)
